cases.html:
Two Basecamp-specific features are worth knowing if status visibility is your main goal:

  • Hill Charts. On any to-do list, you can choose "Track this on the Hill Chart" from the options menu, then manually drag a dot to represent where that piece of work stands. A dot past the peak means the work is "full of certainty, with just execution left," while a dot still climbing means there are unsolved problems or open questions (Basecamp Hill Charts). Every update saves a snapshot to the project's history, and because the status reflects a person's judgment rather than a computer calculation, someone on the team has to actually move the dot for it to mean anything.

Putting it together: an illustrative example

Say a five-person team is redesigning a client's website. As an illustrative setup, they define three milestones — wireframes, visual design, and development — each with a to-do list and a named owner. They turn on a Monday 9am check-in question and put the "visual design" to-do list on a Hill Chart.

By the second week, two of the three design tasks show as dots past the peak, and one is still climbing. That pattern — from the Hill Chart's own logic — tells the team lead that most of the design work just needs execution time, but the remaining task has an open question worth asking about directly, rather than assuming it's simply behind. The dashboard doesn't identify the question; it only shows where attention is needed. The lead still has to follow up with that task's owner.
